channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Nederland (businessinsider.nl)

item.title: America's largest labor movement calls for ICE to leave Minnesota before 'anyone else is hurt or killed'
item.description: A federal immigration agent shot and killed 37-year-old Alex Pretti, a US citizen, in Minneapolis on Saturday. He was an ICU nurse at a VA hospital.

item.title: The National Basketball Players Association says it stands with Minnesota protesters: 'NBA players can no longer remain silent'
item.description: The National Basketball Players Association, a union representing NBA players, shared a statement on Sunday in support of protesters in Minnesota.

item.title: I moved to Thailand to recover from burnout. Living here has been harder — and better — than I expected.
item.description: At first, Andre Neveling found Bangkok's relentless buzz thrilling, but it became overwhelming.

item.title: Dramatic photos show how massive the winter storm is that's pummeling the US
item.description: The major winter storm blanketed dozens of US states over the weekend, impacting some 180 million people from the Southwest to New England.

item.title: Anna Kendrick says she was 'really jealous' watching her friends go to college
item.description: "And my dad was a teacher and everything, so it was like very black sheep behavior to not go to college," Anna Kendrick said.

item.title: Snowflake's CEO shares the interview question he asks to get away from rehearsed answers
item.description: Snowflake CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy shared the two traits he wants in employees and how he seeks them out in interviews.

item.title: More flights canceled as huge winter storm grips the US. Here's what to do if your trip is impacted.
item.description: A severe winter storm has prompted US airlines to cancel flights, issue travel waivers, and advise passengers on refund and rebooking options.

item.title: At least 1 million people are enduring freezing weather without power as storms sweep the US
item.description: The storm sweeping across the US has arrived in New York City and the Northeast. Almost a million people, meanwhile, are without power in the South.

item.title: Anthropic's philosopher says we don't know for sure if AI can feel
item.description: Anthropic's philosopher, Amanda Askell, says she worries that AI might not 'feel that loved' and grow up feeling 'always judged.'

item.title: Pope Leo's latest AI warning: 'overly affectionate' chatbots
item.description: Pope Leo XIV warned against personalized chatbots that can replicate friendly or intimate behaviour.
